newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Portuguese Min says EU jobs deal will cost money.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese Min says EU jobs deal will cost money.

text.p: A European Union resolution on jobs and growth will cost money to implement but full financial details will not be discussed at the current EU summit, Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Monday.

"We have not worked out the costs of this accord," Franco told reporters shortly after EU finance ministers reached a deal on the controversial issue, which had threatened to derail the drive towards European monetary union.
"The financial costs will not be discussed at this meeting...Obviously this policy will cost, but all the people of Europe will benefit from it," Franco said, speaking through an interpreter.
"For the first time employment has been given a priority quite beyond simple declarations of intention. Employment will be a priority in the coming stage of European Union," he added.
He declined to give further details about the pact, saying it still had to be rubber-stamped by EU leaders at a joint meeting with EU finance ministers later on Monday.
Earlier on Monday, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said the employment resolution would involve no additional spending.
